cluster_micro

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_micro_tracing_latency intra_scale Being flagged as a known contact starts the tracing process, and the timing of that flag shapes the observed latency to quarantine.
p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale A known-contact flag can directly lead to quarantine once tracing completes, increasing quarantine-state occurrence.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load upward Known-contact flags are the trigger for quarantine; the layer-specific contact degree of newly quarantined flagged agents defines the tracing workload per index, so more flagged agents in a layer increase the layer's per-index contact load.
p5_micro_tracing_latency → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Longer known-contact-to-quarantine latency plausibly delays quarantine onset for the affected agent.

p5_micro_tracing_latency → p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion upward When individual tracing delays are long and uneven, newly quarantined index agents may accumulate different numbers of active layer contacts before isolation; this uneven accumulation can widen the cross-layer dispersion of per-index contact load.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward A higher per-edge rate of known-contact transitions means contact tracing is yielding more flagged contacts in that layer, raising the probability that an individual agent becomes a known contact.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward When a layer generates many known-contact transitions per edge, tracing workload in that setting may rise, delaying the known-contact-to-quarantine interval for individual agents.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward Higher known-contact incidence per edge in a layer means more contacts are flagged and subsequently quarantined, raising the probability that an individual in that layer is quarantined.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale A higher known-contact rate per layer edge implies more tracing follow-up per edge, raising per-index contact load.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_macro_quarantine_coverage upward Layer-level tracing yield converts more flagged contacts into quarantined agents, increasing population quarantine coverage.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence upward Higher known-contact incidence per layer edge increases the standing caseload of known contacts at the population level.
p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward Heavy layer-level index load can make contact flagging less complete or slower, affecting an individual’s known-contact state.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward Higher per-index contact load in a layer can delay tracing work for individual contacts, increasing their known-contact-to-quarantine latency.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward When per-index contact load is high, quarantine decisions for individual contacts can be delayed or missed, altering individual quarantine status.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale High per-index contact load can strain tracing capacity, reducing known-contact transitions completed per edge in the layer.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward When per-index contact load is unevenly distributed across layers, tracing effort concentrates in high-load settings, delaying the known-contact-to-quarantine interval for individuals whose contacts lie in those congested layers.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Uneven tracing load across layers plausibly lowers known-contact yield in overloaded layers relative to less burdened settings.
p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale Dispersion in layer load reflects high-burden layers where each index plausibly requires more contact work.

p5_macro_traced_per_diagnosis → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load downward When more known contacts are generated per new diagnosis, each index case implies more layer-specific contact investigations, increasing the per-index contact load that must be examined within contact layers.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward When average tracing latency is long, quarantine starts later for newly flagged contacts, reducing the probability that an individual is already quarantined at a given step.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate downward Longer tracing latency slows the conversion of contact edges into known-contact transitions, lowering the per-edge rate of known-contact incidence in each layer.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_macro_traced_per_diagnosis intra_scale Longer tracing latency can reduce the number of newly flagged contacts generated per diagnosis as transmission chains progress before tracing completes.
p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_macro_quarantine_coverage intra_scale Slow tracing delays quarantine placement and can lower the standing quarantine coverage achieved by contact tracing.

p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load downward A higher standing known-contact prevalence increases operational tracing caseload, which can raise the per-index contact load that must be examined within specific layers as newly quarantined agents are processed.
p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence → p5_macro_traced_per_diagnosis intra_scale A larger standing known-contact caseload plausibly changes how many contacts are traced per new diagnosis.
p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence → p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency intra_scale High known-contact prevalence can strain tracing capacity and plausibly lengthen mean tracing latency.
p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence → p5_macro_quarantine_coverage intra_scale More known contacts plausibly lead to more quarantine placements, raising observed quarantine coverage.

N33 | p5_micro_known_contact_flag Agent known-contact state indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: K_i(t) = 1 if known_contact_i(t) = true, 0 if known_contact_i(t) = false; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. N34 | p5_micro_tracing_latency Agent known-contact to quarantine latency Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: Tau_i = date_quarantined_i - date_known_contact_i for agent i, defined only when both native dates are non-null for that agent in the run; undefined otherwise. N35 | p5_micro_quarantine_flag Agent quarantine state indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: Q_i(t) = 1 if quarantined_i(t) = true, 0 if quarantined_i(t) = false; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N36 | p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate Layer known-contact incidence per contact edge Scale: meso | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: r_l(t) = (number of agents i with a known-contact transition at step t, i.e. known_contact_i(t) = true and known_contact_i(t-1) = false, whose layer-attributed record is l) / N_l(t), where N_l(t) is the number of distinct undirected edges in layer l at step t; undefined when N_l(t) = 0 or t-1 is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N37 | p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load Per-index contact load within a layer Scale: meso | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: w_l(t) = (sum over agents i newly quarantined at t of d_i,l(t)) / (number of agents newly quarantined at t), where newly quarantined means quarantined_i(t) = true and quarantined_i(t-1) = false; undefined when no agent is newly quarantined or t-1 is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N38 | p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion Cross-layer dispersion of contact load Scale: meso | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: CV(t) = SD_l(w_l(t)) / mean_l(w_l(t)) over layers with defined w_l(t); undefined when fewer than two layers are defined or the mean is 0. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N39 | p5_macro_traced_per_diagnosis Known-contact transitions per new diagnosis Scale: macro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: P(t) = (number of agents with a known-contact transition at t) / (number of agents with a diagnosed transition at t); undefined when the diagnosis denominator is 0 or t-1 is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N40 | p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency Mean per-agent tracing latency at quarantine start Scale: macro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: Lambda(t) = mean over agents i with quarantined_i(t) = true and quarantined_i(t-1) = false and defined Tau_i of Tau_i; undefined when no such agent has a defined latency. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N41 | p5_macro_quarantine_coverage Quarantine coverage of observed agent-steps Scale: macro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: C(t) = (number of agents i observed at step t with quarantined_i(t) = true) / (number of agents observed at step t); undefined when no agent is observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N42 | p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence Known-contact prevalence share Scale: macro | Phenomenon: tracing_capacity_saturation Definition: K(t) = (number of agents i observed at step t with known_contact_i(t) = true) / (number of agents observed at step t); undefined when no agent is observed.
